lines.text: The richest colony in the world, a revolution of the enslaved, and a nation that has endured ever since. This is the story of Haiti.
On the western third of Hispaniola, France built Saint-Domingue, a colony of sugar and coffee worked by enslaved Africans, the richest in the world.
From the traditions of West Africa, blended with Catholic ways, the enslaved shaped a faith of their own, Vodou, honouring spirits called the lwa.
Toussaint Louverture was born into slavery. He would become the great leader of the revolution.
In 1749 the French founded Port-au-Prince, which would become the capital.
Jean-Jacques Dessalines, also born enslaved, would become the general who finally drove the French out.
And Henri Christophe would fight beside them, and later make himself king of the north.
In 1791 the enslaved rose up. For thirteen years they fought France, Spain and Britain, and destroyed slavery in the colony.
On the first of January 1804, Dessalines declared Haiti independent, the first nation founded by people who had freed themselves from slavery.
In the northern mountains, King Henri Christophe finished a vast fortress, the Citadelle, built to defend the new nation.
From 1822, Haiti ruled the whole island, until the east broke away in 1844 as the Dominican Republic.
A century later, a doctor, Francois Duvalier, became president, declared himself president for life and ruled by terror through his militia.
His son Jean-Claude, known as Baby Doc, took over at nineteen and ruled until he was driven out in 1986.
In 1990, a priest, Jean-Bertrand Aristide, became Haiti's first freely elected president, though coups would follow.
In January 2010, an earthquake struck right beside Port-au-Prince. Much of the city collapsed, and the world sent aid.
Then a long crisis set in, as armed gangs took over much of the capital.
In 2021, President Jovenel Moise was killed in his own home.
In 2024, after the prime minister resigned, a transitional council took charge, trying to steer the country back to order.
Born in the only successful revolt of the enslaved, Haiti's people are still fighting for their future.
